copy.text: How early should I check autopay?

scenes.why: The question as people ask it; the guide carries it because people search it.

copy.text: Work backward from the earliest applicable bank or biller cutoff, then allow extra room for non-business days and processing.

scenes.why: The guide's answer, its first sentence: the plain answer before any detail.

The turn: the product the guide itself hands over to, named and shown on its real screen, captioned with its listing's line closest to what the guide teaches. Screen: "Debt" (What you owe and when it could be gone: totals, a payoff plan worked out from your own numbers, and the debt-free date.) chosen because it is the real screen closest to "Come back anytime. Before bills come out: a US autopay check"; focus on "Total balance, Minimum payments".
Ends on where to read the whole guide, with the product beneath it: the viewer leaves with the next step, not only a pitch.

reasoning.decision: YouTube Short, 1080×1920, 18–45s, hook by 1.2s, sound on
reasoning.because: Search-adjacent audience that will watch a slightly longer explanation if it starts strong. Loops by default.

reasoning.decision: Allowed real lines up to 4 words longer
reasoning.because: Every structure Personal Finance Companion's copy supports at YouTube Short's normal line length is already used by its other films; a longer real line beats telling the same story twice.
